name: Heirloom Blade
blocked_sentences: Whenever equipped creature dies, you may reveal cards from the top of your library until you reveal a creature card that shares a creature type with it. Put that card into your hand and the rest on the bottom of your library in a random order.

needs.what: An op that reveals cards one at a time from the top of a library until it reveals one matching an author-supplied selector (here {"types": ["Creature"], "shares_a_type_with": "subject"}), stops there, moves that one card to a destination (hand), and puts the rest of the revealed cards on the bottom of the library in a random order -- with an unbounded, board-determined scan depth, and no player choice about which card is taken (it is always the first hit). It should also terminate gracefully when the whole library is revealed without a hit, bottoming everything in a random order.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The three existing library-scan ops all fix something this line leaves open. `look_at_top` bounds the pool to `amount` cards off the top -- a constant known when the card is written -- and then lets the player pick any matching card out of that whole window, so it is a bounded tutor, not a first-hit scan; naming a large amount to fake 'until' would reveal and randomize the entire library and let the player choose the best of every match instead of taking the first one. `search_library` looks at the whole library at once (also a chooser, plus rule 701.19's shuffle) rather than scanning down from the top. `cascade` is the only op with the right unbounded top-down shape, but its stop test is hardcoded to 'nonland card with lesser mana value than this spell', it exiles rather than reveals, and it offers a free cast rather than putting the card into hand -- there is no way to substitute a selector for its test. `ripple` has a fixed depth and a hardcoded same-name-as-source test. The trigger half of the line is fine (`dies` with filter `{"attached": true}`, wrapped in `may`), and `shares_a_type_with: "subject"` already exists for the 'shares a creature type with it' clause, so this gap is only the scan.
